frequency_question: How often do central banking principals enact temporary incremental reserve requirements when facing specific liquidity overhangs within a defined multi-month window?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign central banks with statutory mandate over commercial bank reserves implementing temporary, non-standard marginal reserve ratio hikes. Excludes standard permanent changes to baseline reserve requirements.
window: Any designated 4-month operational window subsequent to a liquidity surge event

cases.name: People's Bank of China September 2021 foreign exchange RRR hike
Bank of Russia June 2023 temporary reserve requirement adjustments
Bank Indonesia July 2018 macroprudential liquidity buffer adjustment

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named instances representing the class of targeted marginal reserve tools used by major central banks
known_gaps: Smaller developing economies omitted due to structural differences in monetary transmission
skeleton: 4 major emerging market central bank liquidity management cycles involving targeted marginal reserve adjustments since 2018
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 instances where the structural prerequisite of excess liquidity necessitated action and principals possessed direct authority
validity_reason: Central banking statutory powers and liquidity management toolkits remain stable across multi-year horizons
